title: SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA256 Digest Demonstrator
description: Digests a caller-supplied UTF-8 string or hex byte string with SHA-256, or computes HMAC-SHA256 over it under a caller-supplied hex key, and echoes the algorithm id, entirely offline. It is the live execution surface for the shared guest-safe SHA-256 bundle: the kernel carries the bundle verbatim, so its fixtures and property floor exercise the exact bytes other kernels will later inline. Input is bounded at 64 KiB; an unknown mode or encoding, non-string or non-hex input, a missing or non-hex key, or oversize input is rejected with a closed reason code and no digest. It makes no policy decision and is not a signature scheme: the HMAC key travels in the request.

mode.description: Digest to compute. Defaults to sha256.

input.description: The data to digest: a UTF-8 string, or an even-length hex string when input_encoding is hex. At most 65536 bytes.

input_encoding.description: How input is read as bytes. Defaults to utf8.

key_hex.description: HMAC key as an even-length hex string. Required when mode is hmac_sha256, ignored otherwise.

mcp_tool_definition.name: compute_sha256_hmac_digest
mcp_tool_definition.description: Computes SHA-256 or HMAC-SHA256 over a UTF-8 string or hex bytes (at most 64 KiB) and echoes the algorithm id. Rejects bad input with a closed reason code and no digest.

source: authored by SHARED-SHA256-BUNDLE-1 per ACCT-INFRA-KERNELS-BUILD-SPEC.md Sec.0.1 (bundle plus demonstrator) and Sec.4 (composition contract). Expected values are the NIST FIPS 180-4 example messages and RFC 4231 test cases 1 to 7, cross-checked against node:crypto.
